A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe ChatReID, with matching methods and benchmark tables. Neither includes an appendix, although both reference supplementary material. Its absence limits comparison of supplementary experiments and, especially in v3, training-data provenance and implementation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original ChatReID results across ten benchmarks and training-stage ablations in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds model-size results in Table 6 and qualitative comparisons with untuned VLMs in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The documented method retains the three-stage Qwen2-VL pipeline, seven joint-training tasks, decoder replacement after Stage 1, frozen encoder in Stage 3, and gallery filtering with multi-turn retrieval. Renamed stages and newly specified prompts do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The same ten evaluation benchmarks and four principal Re-ID tasks remain. However, v3 replaces v1's named training-source inventory with a reference to unavailable supplementary material, preventing verification of complete training-data coverage. Its newly stated exclusion of DukeMTMC does not establish removal, since v1 does not explicitly report using it.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 2 adds qualitative comparisons against untuned GPT-4o and Qwen2-VL on standard and cloth-changing retrieval. Comparator membership in the retained quantitative benchmark tables is unchanged; corrected or renumbered citations do not introduce additional baselines.

E3.justification: The new model-size experiment evaluates 0.5B, 2B, and 7B models on MSMT17, LTCC, RegDB, and CUHK-PEDES. Figure 2 also introduces untuned-model comparison conditions. The existing benchmark metrics, train/test separation, image-resizing settings, and gallery-filtering procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a model-size sensitivity analysis in Section 4.3 and qualitative failure comparisons for untuned VLMs in Figure 2. The original training-stage ablation is retained unchanged, moving from v1 Table 5 to v3 Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added model-size table follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1 Tables 2–6 match their counterparts in v3 Tables 1–5. New Table 6 reports additional model configurations: for example, MSMT17 Rank-1 is 38.1 for 0.5B and 91.3 for 7B, alongside the retained 2B result of 90.1. Figure 2 adds qualitative outcomes, rather than demonstrating improved performance of the retained configuration.

T1.justification: The uniform gallery-size sampling rule and Equation 1 remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added; the expanded discussion of identity and reasoning is conceptual.

C1.justification: v3 elevates the previously described instruction corpus of over eight million prompts into an explicit main contribution and adds an abstract claim that experiments demonstrate coherent reasoning. It foregrounds text-side-dominated retrieval while retaining the central one-for-all framework, HPT, and ten-benchmark performance claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new size study as supporting a 2B model because larger models incur greater cost with limited gains, attributing this to Re-ID's relative simplicity. It also interprets untuned VLM failures, while dropping v1's explanation linking weak Stage-3-only infrared performance to limited low-illumination training data.

D1.justification: Within the supplied PDFs, documentation of training-data provenance is substantially reduced: v1 Table 1 lists sources and per-dataset statistics, whereas v3 defers this inventory to absent supplementary material and omits attribute-supervision construction details. Conversely, v3 supplies explicit prompts, a 0.5 positive-pair sampling probability, a ResNet-50 filtering example, and a promise to release code, data, and models upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including CLIP-ReID, Instruct-ReID++, and BLIP, and sharpens its positioning against image-feature-dominated retrieval. Several dataset references disappear with the inventory. The main related-work categories and discussion of existing unified Re-ID approaches remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Methodology changes from separate stage sections containing their own data and training descriptions to a consolidated tuning strategy, Data Engine, and training/testing details. Stage terminology, contribution statements, and experimental discussion are revised, and a Broad Impact section is added.

P2.justification: The radar chart moves from Figure 2 to Figure 1. The earlier capability illustration becomes a substantially expanded, full-width Figure 2 with untuned-model comparisons, and Figure 3 gains an architecture schematic alongside a simplified training diagram. The dataset table disappears from the supplied document, a model-size table is added, and retained tables are reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful model-size evidence, qualitative comparisons, explicit prompts, and clearer organization. However, it makes the early-stage training sources and dataset statistics unavailable within the supplied PDF, weakening verifiability while promoting the instruction dataset as a central contribution. With the main quantitative results unchanged and the referenced supplement absent, the gains and documentation losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
